newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH SHARES EXTEND REBOUND INTO SECOND SESSION.
newsitem.headline: CZECH SHARES EXTEND REBOUND INTO SECOND SESSION.

text.p: A late session push by Czech blue chips extended the Prague Stock Exchange's upturn for a second consecutive day on Thursday, despite disappointing 1996 results from the bourse's two most-capitalised banks.
After edging up slightly at the PSE's daily fixing, electrical utility CEZ and petrochemical concern Chemopetrol both posted late gains to boost the PX50 index 2.4 points, or 0.43 percent, to 558.3.
Overall, 188 issues rose on the day, while 192 fell and 164 held steady. Trading was heavy with a total of 2.5 million shares changing hands on turnover of 1.44 billion crowns.
Chemopetrol closed up 40 crowns at 1,380 after its shareholders agreed to a 10 crown per share net dividend for 1996, while CEZ rose 18 crowns to 1,060 on minor volume.
But the day's biggest news focused on the results release of the country's two biggest banks -- Komercni Banka and Ceska Sporitelna.
Both saw 1996 profits rise, but analysts said they were disappointed in the final numbers.
"I'm a little disappointed by the results, especially at Komercni," Martin Nejedly, a banking analyst at Wood and Company told Reuters.
Komercni Banka, the largest commercial bank, said its audited 1996 net profit edged up to 5.24 billion crowns, calculated according to international accounting standards, from 5.1 billion in 1995.
Ceska Sporitelna reported a full year net profit of 1.9 billion crowns, after 263 million the previous year when provisioning for risky loans bit heavily into its bottom line.
While both banks said dividends would rise for 1996, neither reacted very strongly on the bourse floor.
Komercni closed up one crown at 2,450, and Sporitelna edged up two crowns to 309.
